runtime_gate.reason: Existing canonical F-host shared-runner heartbeat remains stale and height_difference_2 guarded operator recovery remains unexecuted.

score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on adopted London Plan/LPG readback and current 2026 City Hall status pages, with explicit separation of policy/design guidance, protected-view context and proposal-specific microclimate/daylight modelling.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy D9 Tall buildings
sources.fact: Tall buildings must be plan-led and only in locations identified as suitable; environmental impacts including wind, daylight, sunlight and temperature must be carefully considered.

sources.label: D9 cumulative and environmental impacts
sources.fact: D9 requires cumulative visual, functional and environmental effects of proposed, consented and planned tall buildings to be assessed rather than treating a single-site height in isolation.

sources.label: Characterisation and Growth Strategy LPG
sources.fact: Adopted 8 June 2023; character assessment and growth strategy should inform whether and where tall buildings may be appropriate.

sources.label: London Housing Design
sources.fact: Housing design guidance prioritises daylight and sunlight quality and links taller forms to the need for appropriate separation and design-led site-capacity testing.

sources.label: City Hall single-aspect homes answer 2026
sources.fact: 27 March 2026 answer reiterates adequate passive ventilation, daylight, privacy and overheating assessment for single-aspect homes and hotter-climate modelling.

sources.label: London Plan Policy HC4 London View Management Framework
sources.fact: Development in designated strategic views must not harm view composition or strategically important landmarks; exact view geometry and proposal form are required.

sources.label: London View Management Framework
sources.fact: Current City Hall page retains the 2012 LVMF SPG as detailed strategic-view guidance while review work proceeds; it is not a generic London-wide height limit.

sources.label: LVMF review funding decision DD2662
sources.fact: 2024 decision funds updated LVMF guidance and confirms current policy basis in HC1-HC4 and D9; review activity does not itself replace adopted policy.

sources.label: Public London Charter
sources.fact: Adopted London Plan Guidance requires new public space to be safe, accessible, inclusive and managed through an evidenced management plan/legal agreement where applicable.

sources.label: Public London Charter status page
sources.fact: Adopted 8 October 2021; public-realm management requirements are separate from building-height or site-capacity entitlement.

sources.label: 2026 Draft London Plan engagement
sources.fact: The next London Plan is under consultation until 15 October 2026; draft tall-building provisions are emerging policy and are not substituted for the adopted 2021 Plan.

sources.label: Draft London Plan 2026 homes/neighbourhoods chapter
sources.fact: Draft tall-residential/public-space provisions include wind-comfort and family-home design considerations; all remain DRAFT on 27 July 2026.

examples.result: D9's 6-storey/18m minimum definition threshold is not treated as a right to build to 18m or above.
A site being in an Opportunity Area or growth location does not replace the plan-led suitable-location and impact tests for tall buildings.
Wind comfort, daylight, sunlight and temperature effects are not inferred from parcel area or building height alone; proposal-specific modelling is required.
Strategic-view policy is applied only with exact protected-view geometry and proposal massing; no generic view penalty is assigned by borough alone.
The 2012 LVMF guidance is retained with its current status while review work proceeds; future/review material is not silently substituted.
Housing Design daylight/sunlight guidance informs design-led capacity but is not an automatic parcel dwelling-capacity calculator.
2026 Draft London Plan tall-building/public-space provisions remain explicitly DRAFT and are not applied as adopted requirements.
No tall-building/design promotion occurs without exact site, adopted policy location, proposal massing and site-specific microclimate/daylight/view evidence.
